raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Inquiry about Tesco's impact on cost structure and potential restructuring charges",
  "main_topics": ["Tesco integration", "Cost efficiency", "Day one impacts", "Cost base"],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": false,
  "contains_forward_guidance": true,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "What about the cost side with Tesco, are we going to see a kind of day one restructuring charge, structural cost action, and how much of the cost base do you think you actually need to keep from Tesco or can it just be pulled onto the existing Barclays system? And most of the existing Tesco cost base kind of disappears?",
  "answer_quote": "You're going to see day one impacts across the P&L. You'll see a day one impairment impact, you're going to see an onboarding of the business more generally. I think what we would envisage with Tesco is you'll see an integration that will happen over a period of time, Robin, simply because, it's a large file, it's a very important client to us. We want to ensure that we have complete continuity of service for those customers. Clearly there will be some capability that they have that we think is very attractive. So, there will be some sort of two-way capability sharing here, but I would expect there to be, and our business case does expect that we would drive some cost efficiency out of this. As the specific levels, we'll obviously update you when we do that completion, we'll give you some views in Q3 and then in Q4, once we've actually completed, then we'll give you more guidance.",
  "reason": "The answer addresses the cost side and restructuring but does not provide specific figures or a clear answer to the question about the cost base from Tesco."
}

data.question_intent: Inquiry about Tesco's impact on cost structure and potential restructuring charges
data.question_quote: What about the cost side with Tesco, are we going to see a kind of day one restructuring charge, structural cost action, and how much of the cost base do you think you actually need to keep from Tesco or can it just be pulled onto the existing Barclays system? And most of the existing Tesco cost base kind of disappears?
data.answer_quote: You're going to see day one impacts across the P&L. You'll see a day one impairment impact, you're going to see an onboarding of the business more generally. I think what we would envisage with Tesco is you'll see an integration that will happen over a period of time, Robin, simply because, it's a large file, it's a very important client to us. We want to ensure that we have complete continuity of service for those customers. Clearly there will be some capability that they have that we think is very attractive. So, there will be some sort of two-way capability sharing here, but I would expect there to be, and our business case does expect that we would drive some cost efficiency out of this. As the specific levels, we'll obviously update you when we do that completion, we'll give you some views in Q3 and then in Q4, once we've actually completed, then we'll give you more guidance.
data.reason: The answer addresses the cost side and restructuring but does not provide specific figures or a clear answer to the question about the cost base from Tesco.
